day_shape: 91 items: US investigating wedding strike in southern Iran that killed 4 and injured 68, IDF says it cleared Hezbollah's Ali al-Taher tunnel complex in south Lebanon, CENTCOM reports 87 vessels redirected under Iran blockade, heavy regime messaging cycle; nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: US wedding strike in southern Iran
threads.summary: Vice President JD Vance said the US is investigating whether American forces struck a wedding in southern Iran that killed four and injured at least 68, with weapons experts telling Reuters the building was likely directly hit by a US munition. Defa Press posted a photo report of a procession for the victims in Kohestan, and Iran's Tasnim reported six additional military deaths from US strikes this week, bringing the toll to at least 13.

threads.label: IDF clears Ali al-Taher tunnel complex
threads.summary: The IDF announced it had completed clearing a strategic Hezbollah underground network beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, describing it as built over two decades, and said forces are working to neutralise it. IRIB countered that resistance forces are still engaged with Israeli troops on the ridge despite Israel's claim of full control.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz blockade and shipping
threads.summary: CENTCOM said that as of 3 September its forces have redirected 87 commercial vessels, disabled 3 and boarded 2 under the US blockade of Iran, while South Korea is reviewing military options to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The Jerusalem Post reported hardline Iranian pressure to sever undersea fibre-optic cables and analyst assessments that US strikes have weakened Iran's ability to mine the strait as oil flows recover.

threads.label: Regime wartime messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted messages vowing to avenge "our children's blood" and citing the nation's "miraculous growth," while Foreign Minister Araghchi rejected criticism from Jordan's foreign minister and Foreign Ministry spokesman Bagheri said Iran's strikes hit only military targets. Defa Press amplified SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei's declared shift in strategy across battlefield, diplomacy and countering economic blockade, alongside Friday-prayer remarks by air defence commander Elahami.

threads.label: Iran domestic repression and dissent
threads.summary: Iran International reported protest detainee Alireza Sepahi faces execution again after being moved to solitary confinement, signs of renewed hijab enforcement on Tehran streets, and a rights group asking German prosecutors to investigate crimes against humanity tied to late-2025 protests. The UN fact-finding mission on Iran urged withdrawal of legislation carrying up to 30 years' prison for foreign contacts, while Trump's renewed call for an uprising drew a trust-gap response inside Iran.

threads.label: Gaza operations and Israeli politics
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Nukhba company commander Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi in a Wednesday strike on Khan Younis, dismantled 30+ weapon production machines in Nablus, and eliminated two who crossed the Yellow Line in northern Gaza. Netanyahu's office released his 7 October 2023 schedule showing he was first informed at 6:30am, and Ben-Gvir unveiled a "Disengagement 710" plan encouraging Gazan emigration.

threads.label: Iran-China ties under scrutiny
threads.summary: Iran's Judiciary Chief met the President of China's Supreme Court and said Iran's will to expand ties with Beijing is "definite," per Defa Press and IRIB, framing China's technology alongside Iran's indigenous capabilities as ground for a new leap. Iran International reported a brief Pezeshkian–Xi encounter in Bishkek has reignited debate in Tehran over how strategic the partnership actually is.

events.title: Women footballers came home under pressure. Now Iran wants them on camera
events.summary: Five months after Iran's women footballers sought asylum in Australia, the football federation has called the squad back into camp, not to train but to film a documentary about what happened there. Some of the players it wants on camera are the ones who came home under pressure.
